must_ask.say: Is the scale greasy and yellow?
Where is it — scalp, eyebrows, sides of your nose, chest?
Does stress seem to make it worse?
How long has this been going on?

history.answer: I've been dealing with these greasy, yellowish flakes and red patches on my scalp and eyebrows that won't go away.
This problem has been coming and going for about two years, but it became much worse over the last two weeks.
The rash is on my scalp, my eyebrows, the sides of my nose, and there is also a patch in the middle of my chest.
They are red patches covered with greasy, yellowish flakes that peel off easily.
It itches quite a bit, especially on my head and around my nose, but it doesn't really hurt or burn.
No, the spots don't vanish in a few hours like hives; they stay in the exact same places all day.
I've had milder bouts in past winters, and over-the-counter anti-dandruff shampoo helped slightly back then, but nothing has helped this time.
No, I haven't had any fever, chills, body aches, or fatigue.
No, my mouth, eyes, and private areas are completely normal with no blisters, sores, or irritation.
No, my skin is not sloughing off, and I don't have any dark purple spots or tender bruises.
No, my lips and tongue haven't swollen, and I haven't had any trouble breathing or swallowing.
No, I haven't started any new prescription drugs, antibiotics, or pain medicines.
No, I haven't switched my skincare products, soaps, makeup, or detergents, and I don't wear costume jewelry.
No, nobody at home or in my classrooms has a rash or any severe itching.
No, I haven't been hiking, had any bug bites, or traveled anywhere recently.
No, I have never had asthma, allergic rhinitis, or eczema as a child.
No, my joints don't ache or swell, and my nails look smooth without any pitting or lifting.
I tried using regular moisturizers and dabbed a little over-the-counter hydrocortisone cream on my face, but the flakes kept returning.
I have been happily married for fifteen years and have never had genital sores or any sexually transmitted infections.
It definitely flares up whenever I am under a lot of stress at school, like during exam grading periods, and during dry cold weather.
I was thinking it might just be really severe dandruff or perhaps some kind of facial eczema.
As a teacher standing in front of students all day, having greasy yellow scales all over my face is terribly embarrassing.
I am hoping you can prescribe a medicated shampoo and cream to clear up the redness and flaking.
I have mild anxiety, which I manage with relaxation exercises, but I have no other medical conditions.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been hospitalized.
I do not take any prescription medications, regular over-the-counter drugs, or vitamins.
I do not have any allergies to medications, foods, or materials.
I have never smoked cigarettes.
I only drink an occasional glass of wine on special occasions, maybe once or twice a month.
I work as a middle school teacher, and I live with my husband and our two children.
There is no history of psoriasis, severe eczema, or skin diseases in my family.
My periods are regular every twenty-eight days with my last one two weeks ago, and there is no possibility of pregnancy.

exam.finding: Alert, well-groomed female in no acute distress with visible flaking across the eyebrows and forehead.
Blood pressure 118/76 mmHg, heart rate 72/min, respiratory rate 14/min, temperature 36.6 C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Erythematous patches with overlying greasy, yellowish scales on the scalp, eyebrows, bilateral nasolabial folds, and presternal chest, without skin detachment or purpura.
Mild retroauricular erythema and fine scale bilaterally without external canal discharge or tenderness.
Conjunctivae are pink and non-injected, and sclerae are anicteric without discharge or lid margin inflammation.
Oral mucosa is pink and moist without ulcerations, mucosal plaques, or pharyngeal injection.
No palpable anterior or posterior cervical, submandibular, or occipital lymphadenopathy.
Fingernails and toenails are smooth without pitting, oil drop discolorations, or onycholysis; joints show no swelling or tenderness.
